subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps — Redwood vs. Vendor X / Vendor Y
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + proposed bake-off plan (Redwood vs Vendor X / Vendor Y)

Hi John —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. I’ve bolded the items we heard as highest priority from your team.

Pain points you shared:
- Sporadic latency spikes on peak traffic windows (often during batch processing and clinical intake periods).
- Cost unpredictability: current provider’s per-token variability and lack of guidance on batching/kv caching.
- Limited observability: hard to tie model regressions to specific deployments or prompt sets.
- Compliance constraints: need SOC2 evidence and data residency controls for patient-related text.

Goals / decision criteria (as discussed):
1) Latency SLO: median <100ms, p95 <250ms for our typical 512-token chat flows.
2) Cost: demonstrable unit economics, target ~30% lower cost-per-1M tokens than current baseline (to make ROI compelling).
3) Model fidelity: parity or better on clinical extraction & instruction-following.
4) Ops & compliance: SOC2 + audit logs + VPC/private deployment options.

Suggested bake-off structure:
- Participants: Redwood (us), Vendor X, Vendor Y.
- Duration: 2 weeks of deterministic runs + 3 days of soak (throughput) tests.
- Test harness: we’ll run your anonymized sample dataset through each vendor; measures: latency distribution, throughput, token cost, and a quality eval (50 representative prompts + gold labels).
- Acceptance tests: cold-start latency, KV/prefix caching impact, and quality A/B tests on extraction accuracy.

Open questions we need from you to kick off:
1) Final list of evaluation contacts (procurement/legal + technical): please confirm Sarah Lopez (procurement) and who will own data ingestion on your side.
2) Shared dataset: will you provide the anonymized JSONL sample by EOD Friday?
3) Any additional non-functional requirements (e.g., TLS profiles, minimum retention windows)?

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-proposal.pdf (outline, timeline, scope).

Proposed next steps:
- Confirm participants and shared dataset by Fri 20 Feb.
- Kickoff call to align test harness and metrics: Tue 23 Feb (proposed).
- Redwood to provide test harness + Drive folder and credentialed access to the evaluation results.

If that aligns, I’ll send a calendar invite for Tue 23 Feb and share the Drive link + HubSpot deal record.

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks John — great, and welcome Sarah.

Short replies to your questions:
- For private test endpoints we typically support one of the following: temporary API keys + IP allowlist, short-lived VPC peering (if you want network-level isolation), or a dedicated private enclave in our Dedicated environment. For the bake-off soak test we recommend IP allowlist + short-lived keys to reduce setup time; Rafael will share the exact instructions.
- Demo recording: attached (link in Drive). I’ve also uploaded a 10-minute clip of the feature walkthrough to the Drive folder.

Kickoff proposal (final):
- Tue Feb 23, 11:00 AM PT — 45-min alignment: confirm dataset, test harness, and success thresholds.
- Deliverables from Redwood prior to kickoff: test harness README, access to Drive folder, initial endpoint configs for smoke tests.

Acceptance tests (short list we’ll run and report back on):
1) Latency: median/p95 on 1k warm requests and on cold-start after idle period.
2) Throughput: tokens/sec under target concurrency.
3) Caching: measured delta with and without prefix/KV caching on sample flows.
4) Quality: extraction F1 on the provided gold labels (target >= baseline).

Attachments: test-harness-README.md (small text file with steps). Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-bakeoff
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

If that works, I’ll send invites and Rafael will prepare the endpoint instructions and the short smoke-test checklist.

Thanks — see you Tue.

–Marissa
